exemplars.label: strong

stage1.text: 1. Average realized price decline (Priority 1 — test first: affects both Lattes and Drip)

children.text: Hypothesis: Loyalty discount reduced avg_price on Lattes ($5.00 to $4.75) and Drip ($3.00 to $2.85), cutting margin by ~3.3 pp
Hypothesis: Pastry avg_price stayed flat at $4.00, so discounting is concentrated in beverages

stage1.text: 2. Variable unit cost increase (Priority 1 — equal driver to price, concentrated in Lattes)

children.text: Hypothesis: Default oat milk raised Latte unit_cost from $4.00 to $4.30 (+$0.30/unit), compressing Latte margin from 20.0% to 9.47%
Hypothesis: Drip supplier switch did NOT change Drip unit_cost ($2.40 in both Q1 and Q2); Drip margin fell only due to avg_price drop

stage1.text: 3. Product mix shift (Priority 2 — minor driver; note total volume alone does not change margin %)

children.text: Hypothesis: Share shifted toward 20%-margin Lattes (1,000 to 1,300 units) and away from 30%-margin Pastries (800 to 600 units), costing ~0.60 pp

exemplars.stage3:
Restore Brew & Co.'s variable margin from 15.38% back above 21% by unbundling oat milk (+$0.35 surcharge or revert to dairy default) and restructuring the loyalty discount to require a pastry bundle.

Diagnosis: Total variable margin fell 7.14 pp (22.52% in Q1 to 15.38% in Q2), while revenue fell 5.55% ($12,700 to $11,995). Price (-3.29 pp) and unit cost (-3.25 pp) were nearly equal drivers, while product mix was minor (-0.60 pp). Lattes are the core problem: switching to default oat milk raised Latte unit_cost from $4.00 to $4.30 while the loyalty discount cut Latte avg_price from $5.00 to $4.75, collapsing Latte margin from 20.0% to 9.47% even as Latte volume grew 30% (1,000 to 1,300). Contrary to expectations, the drip supplier change left Drip unit_cost flat at $2.40; Drip margin fell from 20.0% to 15.79% solely because avg_price dropped from $3.00 to $2.85.

Recommendations:
1. Make dairy the default milk and charge a +$0.35 oat milk add-on (or +$0.30 minimum), recovering the $0.30/unit cost increase on Lattes.
2. Cap the loyalty discount at 5% and apply it only on orders that pair a beverage with a 30%-margin Pastry (reversing the 800 to 600 unit pastry drop).

Risks & Mitigation: Charging for oat milk risks losing price-sensitive Latte volume (which grew +300 units in Q2). Monitor weekly Latte units_sold; if volume drops more than 10% below Q1 levels (<900 units/quarter pace), offer free oat milk exclusively as the loyalty reward tier.

Next Step: Run a 4-week POS test in Q3 tracking weekly Latte unit margin (target >=18%), Drip avg_price (target >=$2.95), and Pastry attach rate (target >=750 units/quarter pace).
